headline: Anthropic says its biology team had no access to a Copenhagen PhD student's conversations with Claude, after he asked whether his unpublished work shaped its discovery.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: there is no evidence for his concern, and the discovery itself dates from 23 Sep 2026.
importance_line: It raises a practical worry for researchers who paste unpublished results into chatbots, though there is no evidence his work was used and Anthropic denies its team had access.
summary: Cult of Mac, citing The Scientist, reports that Anthropic says Claude was not trained on user transcripts and its molecular biology team had no access to the conversations of Mario Rodríguez Mestre, a University of Copenhagen PhD candidate who had worked on the same proteins and shared unpublished manuscripts with Claude; the report finds no evidence that his work played a role. Our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried CNN's report that Mestre says his research describes the same signatures as Anthropic's 23 Sep 2026 announcement that Claude-powered agents found a system in bacteriophages (viruses that infect bacteria) with features resembling CRISPR.
notes: Reply story: Mestre's questioning answers Anthropic's 23 Sep 2026 announcement. Source printed as Cult of Mac because the Yahoo Tech page is a syndicated copy; url is the Yahoo page where text was read.
